Years ago, MacBook models featured a slot that could be used with a cable lock to secure the computer to a desk leg or similar object. Such slots were most useful at a coffee shop when you wanted to walk to the counter to order another drink without carrying your laptop.

Those slots have long disappeared, but adapters can now be purchased to provide locking functionality for your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro……

Users who remember the security slots embedded in the side of the MacBook have probably been using the machines for quite some time. These slots were designed for T-shaped accessories — you would thread the accessory through the slot and rotate it 90 degrees to lock it in place. The most common design was a cable loop that could be wrapped around a table leg at a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock is now bringing back the concept, launching an adapter that can be mounted on the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design, with screws clamping the adapter onto the MacBook.

The company has now added a version for the MacBook Neo, in addition to its existing models for the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro.

It must be emphasised that this type of lock has always been a very low level of security — its only purpose is to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and running off in a matter of seconds. I would happily use one in a smaller coffee shop, where I could still see my table when I went to the counter to get another tea, but I would never rely on it to let my MacBook out of my sight.

The adapter costs a not-insubstantial $70, and you still need to buy the lock separately, but if you have one lying around in a drawer, you might think it worth getting out and putting it back to use.
